controls.label: Shape
controls.qualification: A sphere of the published radius, lit by Amansinaya; the neutral gray is a display convention, not a measured color.
controls.notes: No image or color of WASP-34 b is published: the sphere has its measured size, and the gray marks an unresolved surface. The lighting is its own star's, at the measured orbit. The gray takes the color of wasp-34's light, as its color dataset measures it.

controls.label: Spitzer
controls.qualification: Published fit · May et al. (2022) · a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve of 3-8 November 2020 · longitude only
controls.notes: Brightness temperature at 4.5 µm of WASP-34 b from May et al. (2022)'s published fit to a Spitzer IRAC 4.5 µm phase curve of 3-8 November 2020. Their Fourier series becomes a map of longitude through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, so there is no north-south detail and every latitude is drawn alike. The hottest longitude is 35° east of noon. Longitudes where the fit gives no emission are left blank. The false color runs from 300 to 1,300 K. With shadows on, the star's light darkens the night half.

charts.alt: The orbits of Amansinaya's planets in this map from above, to scale, with WASP-34 b highlighted and the direction to Earth down. Each orbit is the one the app draws, from the published period, a/R*, eccentricity and argument of periastron; the star is a marker, not to scale.

WASP-34 b crossing its star, as TESS recorded it: 3 sectors (63, 90, 100) of the SPOC pipeline's 2-minute light curves of TIC 437242640, each transit divided by a straight line fitted to the light either side and folded onto the orbit the app draws, then averaged in 8-minute bins. Error bars are each bin's standard error.
